## Part A: Writing exercises (homework)

Practice for after the session.

### A1. Fix the spin
Rewrite each sentence so it says only what the data and the design allow.

| # | Original sentence (from the papers) | Your rewrite |
|---|---|---|
| a | Paper 1 (p.10), primary outcome p = 0.42, difference 13.2 ml/kg (95% CI −15.2 to 41.6): the authors base the case for a larger trial on "the non-significant trend in fluid balance reduction". | |
| b | Paper 2 (p.4): "a positive fluid balance on the first ICU day did not impact the 28-day mortality". | |
| c | Paper 2 (title): "Impact of a cumulative positive fluid balance during the first three ICU days in patients with sepsis …" | |
| d | Paper 1 (p.10): the protocol obtained "the lowest fluid balance on Day 5 ever published". | |

### A2. Climb the verb ladder
Choose the strongest verb each design allows: **was observed in · is associated with · may contribute to · reduced / did not reduce · causes**.

| # | Study | Strongest honest verb |
|---|---|---|
| a | A case series of 12 ICU patients with septic shock who developed pulmonary oedema after large fluid volumes | |
| b | A cohort of 3,000 septic patients: positive fluid balance and mortality, adjusted for severity | |
| c | A single randomised trial of 48 patients: restrictive protocol and day-5 fluid balance | |
| d | Five large randomised trials and a meta-analysis, all consistent | |
| e | A cross-sectional survey of how completely fluid-balance charts are filled in on two ICUs | |

### A3. Write the results sentence (number + CI, no adjectives)
Write one sentence for each, in the style "In [whom], [outcome] was [effect] ([measure] [value], 95% CI [lower] to [upper])".

1. Paper 2, Day-3 cohort: 28-day mortality, positive vs negative fluid balance, HR 1.56, 95% CI 1.10 to 2.22, P = 0.012.
2. Paper 1: death by day 28, 6/24 (restrictive) vs 6/24 (control), relative risk 1.0, 95% CI 0.38 to 2.66.
3. Paper 2, Day-1 cohort: HR 1.17, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.60, P = 0.354.

### A4. A title from your PICO
Formula: **[Design] of [Intervention / exposure] vs [Comparator] in [Population]: effect on / association with [Outcome]**. 10–16 words, design stated, no "impact", "novel", "first".

My PICO: P ______________ I/E ______________ C ______________ O ______________

Working title: ________________________________________________________________

Word count: ____  Design named? ☐  Calibrated verb (association for observational designs)? ☐

## Part B: Manuscript workshop 2: improve your Results section (25 minutes, 20:05)

### How the 25 minutes are used
| Clock | Who | Task |
|---|---|---|
| 20:05–20:10 | Whole class, Q1 | **Numbers**: every number in the class Q1 Results against results pack Q1 |
| 20:10–20:14 | Whole class | **Tables and figure**: title, units, n, abbreviations. Does each stand alone? |
| 20:14–20:19 | Whole class | **Words**: no interpretation, no "trend", no causal verbs |
| 20:19–20:22 | Whole class | **Working title**: design stated, "associated" |
| 20:22–20:30 | You | Run the same checks on your own draft. Write your working title and paste it in the chat |
| By 23:59, Sunday 20 December | You | Final check, then email your Results section |

The improved class Q1 Results are sent as a PDF after the session.

### Final check before you send
- [ ] Every number agrees with your results pack
- [ ] Percentages with denominators, estimates with 95% CIs
- [ ] Crude and adjusted estimates both reported
- [ ] Table 1 and one main table or figure that stand alone
- [ ] No interpretation and no causal words
- [ ] Working title and AI-use statement

### Other sections (taught in 8.1, optional to submit)
If you have time, add any of these in the same file. Trainers give feedback on them.
- **Introduction:** three paragraphs: known, not known, aim
- **Discussion:** answer, compare (e.g. with Paper 2), explain, limitations with their direction, implications, conclusion
- **Abstract:** structured, 250 words or fewer, numbers identical to your Results

## Part C: Getting published (homework)

### C1. Spot the predatory journal

**1. Find the red flags** in this (invented) invitation. How many can you find?

> **From:** editorial.board.gjcmr@freemail.com
> **Subject:** Invitation to publish in our esteemed journal!!
>
> Dear Respected Professor/Doctor,
>
> Greetings! We have gone through your excellent article and are delighted to invite you to submit to the *Global Journal of Clinical Medicine, Nursing, Engineering and Management Research*. We publish all areas of science.
>
> Our journal has an Impact Factor of 9.2 (International Universal Index). We guarantee peer review within 48 hours and publication in 5 days. Processing charges will be communicated after acceptance. Special discount this week only!
>
> Kindly submit your manuscript by replying to this e-mail.

**2. Which journal would you trust?** For each (invented) profile, write *Trust / Check further / Avoid* and one reason.

| Journal profile | Your verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| J1: Indexed in MEDLINE (confirmed in the NLM Catalog), editor names verifiable at universities, fee (APC) shown on the website, median 9 weeks to first decision, uses CONSORT/STROBE checklists. | | |
| J2: Says "indexed in Google Scholar and Index Copernicus", promises acceptance in 72 hours, no fee information, editorial board photos without affiliations. | | |
| J3: Open access, listed in DOAJ, small society journal, no impact factor yet, clear peer-review and retraction policy. | | |
| J4: Its name differs by one word from a well-known journal; the website address is different from the real journal's; it e-mailed you first. | | |

**3. Three checks you can always do:** Think.Check.Submit checklist · DOAJ (Directory of Open Access Journals) · NLM Catalog ("currently indexed in MEDLINE"). You can also ask your librarian.


* * *

### C2. Responding to reviewers

Imagine your own proposed study has been completed and submitted. Write a response row for each comment (thank, answer, say exactly what changed). One of them deserves a polite rebuttal.

| # | Reviewer comment | Our response | Change made (page, line) |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1.1 | "The title says your intervention *improves* outcomes, but this is an observational study." | | |
| R1.2 | "Please report the main result with a confidence interval, not only the p-value." | | |
| R1.3 | "Text and Table 2 give different numbers of patients analysed (212 vs 208)." | | |
| R2.1 | "Please add 1-year mortality." (Your protocol followed patients to day 28 only.) | | |

Tone checklist: ☐ thanked the reviewer ☐ answered every point ☐ said where the manuscript changed ☐ disagreed only with evidence, politely

## Part D: Answer grid: "Be the reviewer" (25 minutes, 21:05)

### What you are doing
Two published papers answer our running question (**fluids in septic shock**) with different designs:

| | Paper | Design |
|---|---|---|
| **Paper 1** | Boulet N, et al. *Crit Care* 2024;28:429 (restrictive strategy targeting non-resuscitative fluids, OPTIFLUID) | Randomised controlled pilot trial, 48 patients analysed |
| **Paper 2** | Hyun D-G, et al. *Ann Intensive Care* 2023;13:105 (cumulative positive fluid balance in the first three ICU days) | Propensity-score-matched cohort from a sepsis registry, 2516 patients |

The whole class appraises **both** papers together. The instructor shows the right page on the shared screen, you vote **Yes / No / Can't tell** in a poll, and a volunteer gives the page and the sentence in the chat. Fill in your own grid as we go. "Can't tell" is a good answer when the paper does not say.

> **Page numbers** are the journal's own page numbers printed at the top of each page ("Page X of 13" for Paper 1, "Page X of 9" for Paper 2). Use the original (unannotated) PDF.

### How the 25 minutes are used
| Clock | What happens |
|---|---|
| 21:05–21:08 | The two papers and the 10 questions (slides). |
| 21:08–21:23 | Whole-class appraisal with polls. Paper 1: questions 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9. Paper 2: questions 4, 5, 8 and 9. |
| 21:23–21:30 | What may each design claim? The side-by-side summary. |
| At home | Answer the remaining questions (1–3, 6 and 10) for both papers. |

### Where to look
| Question | Paper 1 (RCT): pages | Paper 2 (cohort): pages |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Question | Abstract (p.1); last paragraph of Background (p.3) | Abstract (p.1); end of Background (p.2) |
| 2 Design | Title (p.1); "Trial design and oversight" (p.3) | Title (p.1); Methods (pp.2–3) |
| 3 Participants | "Patients" (p.3); flow chart Fig. 1 (p.5); Discussion limitations (p.10) | "Data source and patient selection" (p.2); Results first paragraph (p.3) |
| 4 Comparison groups | "Randomization and blinding" (p.3); Table 1 (p.6) | "Propensity score matching" (pp.2–3); Table 1 (pp.5–6); text p.4 |
| 5 Bias | "Randomization and blinding" (p.3); Discussion (p.8) | Methods (pp.2–3); Discussion limitations (pp.7–8) |
| 6 Outcome | "Outcomes" (p.4) | "Propensity score matching and outcomes" (p.3) |
| 7 Numbers | "Primary outcome" (p.6); Table 3 (p.10) | Abstract (p.1); "Outcomes" (p.4) |
| 8 Words vs design | Abstract conclusion (p.1); Discussion (pp.8, 10); Conclusions (p.11) | Title (p.1); Abstract conclusion (p.1); Discussion (pp.4, 7); Conclusions (p.8) |
| 9 Limitations | Discussion (pp.8–10) | Discussion (pp.7–8) |
| 10 Use | Your judgement (whole paper) | Your judgement (whole paper) |

### Answer grid (one copy per paper)
Paper: 1 / 2

| # | Question (simplified appraisal checklist) | Yes | No | Can't tell | Page | Notes (one line) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Question**: Can you write the study's PICO in one line? | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | | P: … I/E: … C: … O: … |
| 2 | **Design**: What is the design, and is it the right one for the question? | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | | |
| 3 | **Participants**: Who was included, and who was left out? Would your patients have been included? | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | | |
| 4 | **Comparison groups**: Were the groups similar at the start (Table 1)? How was this achieved (randomisation / matching / adjustment)? | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | | |
| 5 | **Bias**: Who knew which group patients were in (blinding)? Could that change the outcome? | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | | |
| 6 | **Outcome**: Was there ONE pre-specified primary outcome, measured the same way in both groups? | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | | |
| 7 | **Numbers**: What is the main result as an effect size with 95% CI? Is the CI narrow or wide? | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | | Effect: ……… 95% CI: ……… |
| 8 | **Words vs design**: Do the conclusions match the design ("associated" vs "caused"; no "trend" for p = 0.42)? | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | | Words found: |
| 9 | **Limitations**: Are the main limitations stated honestly? Name one the authors missed. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | | Missed: |
| 10 | **Use**: Would this change practice in your unit? Why / why not? | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | | |

**My verdict in one sentence:** ______________________________________________

**One thing I would copy into my own proposal:** ______________________________

### Hints if you are stuck
- **Q1:** the PICO is usually in the last paragraph of the Introduction ("we aimed to …"). Is the paper's outcome the same as in our running question (28-day mortality)?
- **Q4:** a randomised trial makes groups similar by chance; a cohort can only match or adjust for what was measured. Find the sentence that says which.
- **Q5:** who decided how much fluid each patient received, and did they know the group?
- **Q7:** look for "difference" or "HR" followed by brackets. Does the interval include 0 (for a difference) or 1 (for a ratio)?
- **Q8:** search for the words *impact, show, trend, ever, regardless*.
